beforeOnly: Good compost making simply involves not throwing away anything of organic origin. Kitchen scraps, hedge trimmings, pet litter, cardboard boxes - a good compost bin will take all you throw at it and ask for more. Good compost will reward you with an abundance of lush, tasty and, above all, cheap food.
afterOnly: Good compost making turns suitable garden and kitchen waste into something useful. Vegetable peelings, hedge trimmings and torn plain cardboard all have a place in the bin. Good compost will reward you with an abundance of lush, tasty and, above all, cheap food.

beforeOnly: Prepare a fine, firm surface and remove competing weeds. Make a drill at the depth given for the crop; water it first if dry. Sow, cover and firm gently, then keep the seed zone moist. On coarse no-dig compost, use a little sieved compost in the drill and over the seed.

Modules in a greenhouse or on a windowsill give early crops a start while outside soil is still cold. Sow at the crop’s depth, label with variety and date, and give the seedlings light and steady moisture. Use modules early in the year; later, a small outdoor nursery bed is often easier than nursing young outdoor crops through a hot greenhouse.
Sow little and often where the crop allows it. Check the individual guide before treating all seeds, plugs or planting depths alike; carrots, lettuces and peas do not start in the same way.
afterOnly: Prepare a fine, firm surface and remove competing weeds. Make a drill (a shallow groove) at the depth given for the crop; water it first if dry. Sow, cover and firm gently, then keep the seed zone moist. On coarse no-dig compost, use a little sieved compost in the drill and over the seed.

Modules are the separate cells in a seed tray. In a greenhouse or on a windowsill, they give early crops a start while outside soil is still cold. Sow at the crop’s depth, label with variety and date, and give the seedlings light and steady moisture. Use modules early in the year; later, a small outdoor nursery bed is often easier than nursing young outdoor crops through a hot greenhouse.
A station is one sowing or planting position. Sow little and often where the crop allows it. Check each guide’s method and depth; carrots, lettuces and peas do not start in the same way.

beforeOnly: Grow early lettuce or spinach while the summer plants are still small. Seed trays can occupy staging before the young plants move outdoors. When growing plants for later planting outdoors, use the earlier planting dates from the crop guides.
When summer crops finish, clear them and use the space for suitable autumn lettuces or other salad leaves. Choose varieties for the season; an unheated greenhouse still gets cold at night.
afterOnly: Grow early lettuce or spinach while summer plants are small. Seed trays can occupy staging. Use the crop guide’s protected sowing dates for raising plants; harden them off and plant outdoors when the weather and soil suit the crop.

Raise suitable autumn lettuces or Oriental leaves before the summer crops finish, within their sowing windows (pages 56–59). Clear spent crops and plant the replacements. Choose varieties for the season; an unheated greenhouse still gets cold at night.
